source.title: A Quantitative Experimental Repeated Measures Study of Training Dynamics in a Small Llama Style Language Model Under a Compute-Aware Token Budget

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a single-model token-training trajectory with an early fall and later rise in validation loss, challenging an unqualified expectation of continued loss reduction. It does not fit scaling laws or test their exponents.
record.gate_note: The reported validation-loss trajectory bears on V1 and the curve-bending part of V7. Validation perplexity, volatility, backslides, and seed variability are not separate rows because they do not measure the loss scaling named in the versions. The study cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al.; their results are not extracted as this study's findings.
record.test_reason: This is a training-dynamics study of one 4.26M-parameter model trained once per seed to about 20M TinyStories tokens. Parameters, data size and compute are never varied across runs, and no power law is fitted or extrapolated. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as background on diminishing returns. The within-run rise in validation loss after about 4M tokens happens under a fixed learning-rate schedule, and the author attributes it to corpus repetition, schedule and budget. That is overfitting or instability outside V1's conditions (other factors not a bottleneck; Kaplan's L(D) uses early stopping). It is not a test of a scaling curve. V7's bending refers to scaling curves across runs or fits, not to regression inside one run. So the study does not bear on any version, and the finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The author concludes that in this constrained run, early rapid improvement gave way to recurrent regression with no stable phase. Evaluation should therefore track trajectories, not only endpoints. The author limits the finding to this small model, fixed corpus and configuration, and suggests it may reflect model size, corpus repetition, learning-rate schedule and token budget.
record.recipe_differences: One small model is trained on a fixed token schedule and validation loss is tracked over intervals; the study does not conduct a multi-model, multi-token scaling sweep or fit the original scaling-law relationships.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors suggest the observed behavior may reflect interactions among model size, corpus repetition, learning-rate schedule, and token budget; these factors were not varied in this study.

fits_no_version.finding: A 4.26M-parameter Llama-style model on TinyStories (6 seeds) reaches its minimum validation loss, 2.7996, at about 4M tokens. Loss then rises monotonically to 3.9010 at 20M tokens, and backslides recur.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small compute-constrained single runs, validation loss can regress with continued token exposure (overfitting or instability), so per-run trajectories can diverge from the assumption that loss keeps falling with more data.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one 4,262,144-parameter model, one fixed corpus, six seeds, and one constrained training configuration. There is no scaling sweep, power-law fit, or test of parameter/compute allocation; the authors also note the limited seed count and compute setting.
record.rows_left_out: Validation perplexity, rolling volatility, backslide frequency, and stable-phase summaries are omitted because they do not directly measure validation-loss scaling. Other interval values are not tabulated individually in the text; the selected intervals and the reported qualitative trajectory are retained.

untested.parts: All of it: no variation of parameters, data or compute across runs, and no power-law fit.
All of it: no comparison of fits, exponents or compute-optimal splits, and no scaling curve across runs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked within-run checkpoint losses to V1 and V7 and labelled them challenges and supports. These are reassigned: a single model's training curve with rising validation loss does not measure the scaling relationship, which is defined across model, data or compute sizes. The rows are kept as context, each with versions ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: Only token exposure is observed, for one small model and one fixed corpus. The study does not vary parameters or compute, establish that other factors are not bottlenecks, fit a power law, or test behavior over several orders of magnitude.
The study shows a non-monotonic token-training curve, but does not test dependence on fitting choices, compare published exponents or compute-optimal splits, or fit alternative curves.
